#4088. Marvel Cosmic Invasion's Doctor Doom-Themed DLC Gives It The Post-Game Tail It Was Missing

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a new brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on quickly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his plan.

As for the new playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

As you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with new special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

Beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds new palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

#4087. "I Don't Feel This Is A Good Direction" - Chrono Trigger Composer Thinks It's Time To End Dragon Quest

"it’s no longer possible to create anything new"

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda has posted a blog in which he states it might be time for the Dragon Quest series to end.

As covered by our pals over at Time Extension, Mitsuda-san believes that without Akira Toriyama – who sadly passed away in 2024 – the Dragon Quest franchise cannot continue imitating the iconic artist's signature style.

The catalyst for this comment was the release of a new mobile game titled Dragon Quest RPG: The Cursed Tree And the Chosen Isle, which features artwork strikingly similar to Toriyama-san's work.

“Dragon Quest RPG‘s Toriyama-san-styled illustration has become a hot topic, but for the illustrator, for Akira Toriyama fans, and for the now-deceased Akira Toriyama himself, I don’t feel this is a good direction for everyone involved. In my personal opinion, since it’s no longer possible to create anything new no matter how hard one tries, it might be time to end the Dragon Quest series, and for Yuji Horii to create a new RPG. (There are a lot of remakes out there, after all).”

Online speculation, highlighted by Power Up Gaming, also points at the potential involvement of generative AI to create the in-game characters. However, despite enthusiasm around the technology from creator Yuji Horii, there's doesn't seem to be any legitimate evidence that this is the case.

Regardless, Mitsuda-san does have a point. Dragon Quest is synonymous with Toriyama-san's art style, and it might be tricky to maintain this without the man himself at the helm. Indeed, reaction to Dragon Quest XII: Beyond Dreams hasn't exactly been universally positive, with some online users criticising the design of the main protagonist.

We think it's unlikely that Dragon Quest will end anytime soon, however. The series is still incredibly popular to this day, and continues to sell ludicrous numbers in Japan especially. Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World is scheduled to release on Switch 1 and 2 on 3rd December 2026.

#4086. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4085. Marathon’s Symbiosis Update Adds Host Of New Modes, Including Permanent PvE, Next Month

Bungie has detailed its upcoming Symbiosis update for Marathon, which introduces several significant modes next month. Chief among them is the new permanent PvE mode, which Bungie previously experimented with and promised earlier this year.

Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success.

The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.

Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15.

The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP.

For more on Marathon, check out our review.

#4084. GTA 6 Cheat Codes Are Already Out There, And Here’s All of Them

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

The wait for Grand Theft Auto 6 is almost over. Rockstar's long-awaited open-world adventure launches on November 19, and the first reviews are already rolling in, with the game currently sitting at a staggering 99 on Metacritic, tying the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the highest score in the site's history.

But while most players are still getting ready to explore Leonida for the first time, some fans are already thinking about a much more important part of the GTA experience: cheat codes. And, perhaps unsurprisingly, they are already circulating online!

According to GTA Base, a well-known resource among Grand Theft Auto fans, there are already 61 cheats cataloged for GTA 6. They cover everything from getting extra cash and spawning vehicles to changing the weather and applying bizarre visual filters. But there's one catch: you won't be able to use any of them until you finish the main story. So yes, Rockstar really wants you to earn your chaos this time.

Unlike previous entries, GTA 6 doesn't let you activate cheats right from the beginning. First, you need to complete the story, which unlocks the Cheats section under Progress Menu. Each cheat also has its own requirement, so simply knowing a button combination isn't enough.

Once you've unlocked the cheat you want, bring up your in-game phone, hold L1 + R1 on PlayStation 5 or LB + RB on Xbox Series X|S, and enter the corresponding combination using the D-pad. Interestingly, all the sequences use directional inputs, meaning the codes are identical on both platforms.

Unlike previous entries, GTA 6 doesn't let you activate cheats right from the beginning. First, you need to complete the story, which unlocks the Cheats section under Progress Menu.

One more thing before you start turning Vice City upside down: using cheats disables Trophies and Achievements, as well as the ability to save your game! So make sure you have a clean save before experimenting.

GTA Base just proved how quick they are and has already put together an impressive list of 61 cheats, organized into five categories. Not all of them have been fully discovered just yet, though, so some button combinations are still missing!

We've included everything known so far, along with what each cheat does and its code whenever it's been confirmed. We'll keep updating this article as more combinations pop up, so be sure to check back if you're planning to cause some trouble in Vice City.

Rockstar is known for putting insane levels of detail into their games, but here is how they are going above and beyond with GTA VI.

GTA VI will be one of the biggest video game releases in our lifetimes, and it will be talked about for years to come.

For the latest updates and any newly confirmed combinations, check out GTA Base's PS5 cheat guide and Xbox Series X|S cheat guide. With the game launching tomorrow, it probably won't take long for players to start uncovering the remaining codes. Just remember to finish the story first!

#4083. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4082. Every MTG Universes Beyond Crossover Set, Ranked

Wizards of the Coast originally released Magic: The Gathering crossovers at a slow and steady pace, but four Universes Beyond sets have dropped in 2026, meaning the floodgates have well and truly opened, for better or worse. Luckily this isn't the norm, and there will be an even split of Universes Beyond and in-universe sets moving forward, currently slated to be three of each every year.

If you're looking for a comprehensive guide to all the Universes Beyond sets and major drops, including Commander precons, listed in order from worst to best, then we've got you covered. Each set is ranked based on originality, card quality, interest in the release, and the impact of the cards on the MTG landscape (in the case of Commander/Standard set releases).

Updated on November 18, 2026 by Niall Walsh: Star Trek is out now, and it's certainly not getting the best reception from players or critics, but it brings the 2026 release schedule to a close, at least in terms of full sets. We know we have three more Universes Beyond sets coming next year, but only one has been revealed so far...

Where do we even begin with the Spider-Man set? This disaster of a release didn't even make it to MTG Arena at first because of licensing issues, which led to widespread confusion in the community. On top of that, what was supposed to be a smaller set became a full Standard release, resulting in cards that felt rushed and uninspiring and that didn't synergize well with existing Standard sets or function well as a standalone product.

The straw that broke the camel's back was the fact that this set ended up pushing back the release of Lorwyn Eclipsed, a hugely anticipated original MTG set, and it came in the middle of a major ramp-up in new products, leaving players feeling burnt out and slighted by the expectation to invest in new products so often.

Magic: The Gathering has plenty of mechanically unique cards that have only seen one printing and there's no guarantee that they'll be reprinted.

It very nearly fell to the bottom of the pile, but the Star Trek set just about manages to come in ahead of Spider-Man... for now. This list is fluid, so time may treat Star Trek worse than it did Spider-Man, but Star Trek's immediate legacy in Magic: The Gathering is a set that was almost universally panned for one reason or another.

While we had fun during prerelease, the set isn't having much impact on the Standard meta beyond a few cards like The Naked Time, and many core Magic fans disdain sets where the artwork depicts real-life actors playing roles we've seen on screen. It makes for a set that lacks creativity in the art department, and compared to sets like Reality Fracture and even The Hobbit, the gap is huge.

Availability was also a nightmare for Star Trek, with stock for the set still not with some retailers almost a week after release, which is having a knock-on effect for players.

One saving grace for Star Trek is its mechanics. Assimilate is cool, as is Strange New Worlds, and the return of Spacecrafts is welcome; if you can ignore the artwork and card names, this does have an Edge of Eternities 2 feel to it. Its Commander decks are 50/50, with the Borg and Landing Party decks being by far the strongest and most popular of the four, but that's not to say the Klingon and Federation decks are useless; they're just not as good in direct comparison.

The Universes Beyond Doctor Who release brought with it four very strong Commander decks, each one designed around several iterations of The Doctor and their villains. The main release also came with three Secret Lairs: Dalek Lands, Weeping Angels, and Regeneration.

Despite the initial reaction to these Commander decks, some have become shelf fodder and are often available below MSRP. This sometimes happens when a product just isn't as widely appealing once its release window passes, or when the deck's reprint value is poor.

A sort of mini-set within the greater Universes Beyond collection, the Assassin's Creed Universes Beyond contains 100 cards split across Beyond Boosters, a Starter Kit, a Bundle, and Collector Boosters, as well as two Secret Lairs. Beyond Boosters are a new type of Booster pack, and are not draftable but contain a mix of older cards with new artwork and original new cards designed with the Assassin's Creed games in mind.

The main thing working against Assassin's Creed is that it was released in the Eternal-only window for Universes Beyond, and this limited its potential to an almost redundant state. If given the proper Universes Beyond treatment in 2026, an Assassin's Creed set would be infinitely better and more relevant, but instead, this release is often forgotten.

The TMNT Universes Beyond set's one major redeeming quality is its draftability. It's a fun set to draft, but beyond that, it has a minimal impact on Standard and Commander.

Artistically, the set was perfect for the property it represented, and it even had some very cool chase cards in the form of the Kevin Eastman Borderless Signature turtles, but as a Magic set, especially one legal in the Standard format, TMNT is a letdown.

What has worked well and truly against TMNT is that it is sandwiched between two highly anticipated sets, Lorwyn Eclipsed and Secrets of Strixhaven, and both ended up being absolute blockbusters, making TMNT look meek in comparison.

This is easily one of the most divisive releases in Magic: The Gathering history, but at its core, it's shaping up to be a strong release in a few key ways. It's a highly draftable set, even if some of the ten combos are quite a bit stronger than others; it's still a fun set to build Limited decks with. Its Commander precon decks are also fairly impressive, with even the weakest of the decks being easily upgradable.

There are still four more Marvel-themed sets expected to be released in order to complete the full set of Infinity Stones.

The impact of this set on Standard and Commander in general will form over the coming months, and the result of this may change the ranking considerably, but for now, the Marvel Super Heroes set is trending far more positively than we expected, and it's going to make Wizards of the Coast a truckload of money.

The extremely popular Fallout series joined Magic: The Gathering with four Commander decks. The four decks follow a different faction or characters from the games, including Caesar and his Legion, the various mutants that populate the wastes, and even your favorite companion, Dogmeat.

In 2026, these decks are highly sought after and, for the most part, quite valuable. Fallout is a very popular property, so this was expected, but the limited nature of these Commander decks has led to some artificial pricing, especially given the overall power of some of the decks; it's all a bit disproportionate.

Regardless, the decks are well-built and themed, so if you can get your hands on one, they're a lot of fun to play with.

Love it, hate it, or simply don't care about it, the Avatar MTG set surpassed all expectations upon release in 2025 and was easily one of the most impactful Universes Beyond sets ever released, with the 2025 World Championship-winning deck largely featuring cards from the set in the Izzet Lessons archetype. Two of its biggest cards, Gran-Gran and Badgermole Cub, just got banned in Standard, too.

For Avatar fans, this set was a dream come true; for those with no attachment to the IP, it was a completely inoffensive crossover that produced unique card designs that became highly desirable in the print version of the game.

The Commander offering left a little to be desired, with no pre-con decks released, and a Commander's bundle available instead.

Given its smaller size, The Hobbit isn't going to leave the same lasting impression as the Tales of Middle-earth set, but that doesn't mean it isn't packed with exciting cards, a decent draft experience, and some big Commander additions and reprints. It feels like a continuation of the previous Lord of the Rings set, only this time it's Standard-legal.

The lack of any Commander precons was disappointing, as was the general size of the set, but given that this was turned around less than three years following the release of Tales of Middle-earth, it's actually quite an impressive feat.

Time will tell whether this set has any major impact on the Standard format, but we don't foresee any groundbreaking archetypes rising from the set. However, be sure to keep an eye on Goblins and Dwarves, both of which just got much more playable in Standard with the release of this set.

Any Middle-earth sets are going to rank highly just because they feel like a true Magic-adjacent property, and the cards always look and play great for the most part.

The Final Fantasy Universes Beyond crossover ended up being a huge hit with FF and MTG fans alike, largely because it was so clear to everyone that a lot of thought and planning had gone into the releases, and in reality, it was a hugely relevant deck in Standard at the time of release, with some powerful Mono-Green landfall and Gruul landfall decks still floating around using a few standout cards from the set.

On the Commander front, the FF VI Revival Trance deck is a major standout as one of the best Commander pre-con decks ever released, both out of the box and with minor upgrades.

There's a reason why this is the best-selling Magic set of all time, and while many purists may cringe at this fact, Final Fantasy will influence why Magic is the way it is for years to come.

#4081. Surprising Literally Nobody, Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Most Pre-Ordered Game In PlayStation And Xbox Store History

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19. You can preload the game on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S starting today, as detailed by Rockstar Games, PlayStation, and Xbox. Alongside this announcement, both PlayStation and Xbox have revealed that – surprise! – GTA VI is the most preordered game in the history of their respective digital stores.

That's not shocking – GTA VI is, by many metrics, the most anticipated game in history, with its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, selling nearly 235 million copies since its launch back in 2013. There's also the fact that Rockstar Games is not releasing a physical edition of GTA VI, per se. Yes, you can go to a store to pick up a GTA VI box (and you can do so today, allowing you to preload the game), but inside that box will be a download code for a digital version of the game – you won't find GTA VI on a physical disc. So, naturally, many players are opting to purchase the game on digital storefronts like the PlayStation and Xbox game stores.

"Grand Theft Auto VI, the most preordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store, launches November 19," an Xbox blog post reads. "Considering the unprecedented demand, we encourage everyone to begin preloading as soon as possible to ensure you're prepared for launch day." PlayStation echoes this statement with a blog post of its own that reads, "Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most preordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store. Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start preloading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day."

There you have it: People are very excited about Grand Theft Auto VI.

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. #4080. Review: TANUKI: Pon's Summer (Switch 2) - Cosy Postie Delivers Sick BMX Tricks & Minigames

The gaming calendar is busier than it’s been in recent memory. We’re wedged between the Ocarina of Time remake and GTA 6, having only just recovered from the onslaught of games that launched in September. The prospect of picking up another right now might not be an inviting one, but if any game could do it, it’s Tanuki: Pon’s Summer.

This quiet, cosy, understated gem has really launched at the perfect time. Playing as the titular Tanuki, you’re tasked with getting a shrine ready for a big festival towards the end of the summer. You have to raise funds for repair work, and find folks in town who can actually carry it out. To do so, you pick up a delivery job, get to know all of your eccentric neighbours, and pull off some sick BMX tricks along the way.

That sounds simple, but this is just the ramp used to propel you into the ridiculous amount of tasks you can get up to in Tanuki: Pon’s Summer. While primarily all about riding a BMX and delivering parcels, you quickly realise that this is a simulation game with a vibrant, animated world that invites exploration.

A quirk of the delivery outfit you work for is that you don’t just deliver the mail. No, you are the backbone of society. The job isn’t over until the customer has a smile on their face. So, if your round takes you to a local fisherman, and he’s feeling down about how he isn’t getting enough business, it’s your job to cheer him up and try out some fishing yourself. If you’re dropping a parcel off at a bar, and the place is packed, you better get ready to pull pints. If a photographer is lacking inspiration, then you have to pick up a camera and help her find it.

You get the point; Tanuki: Pon’s Summer manages to pull off so many wildly different minigames with ease, and (mostly) without losing its identity. When you park up the BMX to play some baseball, it feels like you’re diving further into this gorgeous world, rather than stepping into a different game entirely.

It feels like the idea behind these minigames is that they’re not supposed to overstay their welcome, but I found myself sorely wishing I could return to a few of them. The golf minigame towards the end in particular is one of the best golf sims going. The same goes for bar work; trying to replicate the drinks being ordered was satisfying and moreish, but gone too soon and never playable again. If anything, developer Denkiworks misses a trick in not giving you some kind of game mode that lets you play through these on a loop - I would have happily dived back in for that.

This is not to say that every minigame is pulled off with ease. There are some that just don’t work, and were more of a frustrating slog than anything else. The good thing is that this is a cosy game with low stakes, so if you’re struggling with one of them, there’s almost always a way to make things more generous, or skip over it if you fail enough times. But at times, this can feel like a cop out; the few frustrating minigames could have been improved rather than skipped over.

Unfortunately, the worst game of the bunch doesn’t even let you skip it, at least in my playthrough. This involves you transporting boulders in a cave, rolling them through an obstacle course.

To understand the issue with this, you have to understand that Tanuki: Pon's Summer doesn’t do precise controls. The opening makes this clear when you’re taught how to use the BMX - everything is simplified, and you’re not expected to do anything too intricate. Pon moves around too sluggishly and ragdoll-y for that to work. And for the most part, the game is built around this.

The cave minigame forgets this entirely. Pon has to pilot the boulders through tight walkways, often fighting against the game’s physics to avoid falling off the ledge. If you do fall, you go right back to the beginning, losing all progress. I got through it, but I worried for the state of my Joy-Con afterwards, with how much stress they were put through.

Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is at its best when it’s as difficult as you want it to be. You can try and pull off some tricks in golf to beat your opponent, or play it safe and have her win. You can make a lousy bartender and call it a day, or you can throw your all into it. You can rack up as many points on the BMX as you like, or ride slow and steady. But when a minigame just can’t find its footing, like riding the boulders in the cave, the game loses track of what makes it work.

At times, it can also feel that the game spreads itself a little too thin. I felt this most in the basic base building. You can unlock a whole lot of items to revamp the Tanuki shrine, but you can’t do too much with them. There’s just not enough freedom, so the plots of land became more of a dumping ground for my trophies.

Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is a cosy game that understands what it means to be a cosy game: create a gorgeous world you want to get lost in, with satisfying but lower-stakes gameplay. By the time I had rebuilt the Tanuki shrine and completed Pon’s summer job, I wanted to dive back in and see more of the townsfolk I’d met along the way. I wanted to keep delivering their mail and nosing my way into their business.

But there were a few sequences in the game I was happy to see the back of, either because they were on the duller side, or just didn’t work with the exaggerated, slapstick control scheme. Equally, I wish Pon’s Summer spent longer on what it does right, letting us go on an infinite number of deliveries around the island, or play as much golf as we please.

#4079. Rockstar President Breaks Silence Ahead of GTA 6 Launch

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

Given the mad fervor with which the universe as we know it is preparing for the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 tomorrow, I don’t think it’d be hyperbolic to call Rockstar the, er, rockstar of video game development. Even if its games take a hot minute to come out, they’re always bangers when they do, and both the industry and the gaming public naturally hang upon their every word in a manner not dissimilar to someone like Mick Jagger.

Even so, not everyone who works at Rockstar is the kind of person who seeks out the public eye. Take, for example, Sam Houser, who is both the president of Rockstar and the executive producer of GTA 6. Houser has worked on the GTA series in some capacity since its very first title in 1997, but unlike some of the company’s more front-facing divisions and employees, he has always had a tendency to keep his head down and just let the games speak for themselves.

However, with such a major landmark title like GTA 6 quite literally on the horizon, the president of the company bringing it is at least informally obligated to share a few words, and that’s exactly what Houser did in a brief, yet poignant statement shared with IGN.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

As Houser explained to IGN, the predominant belief that spurs Rockstar’s developmental ethos forward is that games can be just as poignant of a medium of storytelling as any other, whether it be film, television, or print. Not only that, but games, in their ideal form, can become a vital component of the modern cultural zeitgeist and give rise to settings and characters that stick with us long after the fact.

This firm belief has culminated in the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 after 13 long years of development. “While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special,” Houser said.

He added that, whether someone is experiencing the GTA series for the first time or has been with it since the very beginning, the game’s world and the narrative contained within it is meant to be shaped by player interaction.

We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of.

“We hope it felt both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope that you had fun. We are incredibly grateful to you and everything that you do to celebrate games. We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you,” Houser concluded with a word of thanks.

Obviously, every professional game developer out there wants their product to be well-received, both so it makes back the money invested into it, and so that it really sticks with the players who experienced it. Grand Theft Auto 6 may not technically be out yet, but even ahead of release proper, I’d say it’s well on track to meeting and exceeding Houser’s hopes.

For one thing, just this morning, the embargo officially broke on the game’s critical reviews, and perhaps unsurprisingly, GTA 6 has received the official seal of being the hottest thing since toasted bread, both from our own Steve Hannley and pretty much everyone else. Its Metacritic reviewer average has reached 99, tying it with one of the most highly-reviewed games of all time, the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which is kind of amusing considering the remake of that game just came out.

As for cash, well, it’s difficult to say for certain without hard numbers, but pre-release projections had the game netting its publisher, Take-Two Interactive, a stunning $3.5 billion in revenue, and considering the number of people planning on skipping work to play on launch day, I’d say that’s a fairly realistic figure.

#4078. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

#4077. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business Review - Delivering Where It Matters

Australia Did It: End-of-the-world Railway Defense Business is a game I catch myself playing in my head long after I shut it off. Though it uses turn-based strategy as its base, it expands beyond the genre’s regular confines, blending elements from roguelikes, puzzle games, bullet-heaven titles, and the tower-defense genre. The result is an experience that demands wide-scale experimentation and rewards improvisation.

In a post-apocalyptic world where the Atlantic Ocean has dried up, you risk your life to ensure your shipment reaches its destination. Riding from station to station by train, you must build your team amid your many missions as various mutated creatures, malicious machines, and coordinated soldiers attack your convoy. Lore is doled out piecemeal and serves mostly as background dressing, but each time I learned more about the world, I became more curious.

To survive the harshness of the wasteland, you must use cindermint, an in-game resource gained for surviving turns and killing enemies, to spawn defenders, with three base classes to choose from. The revolver-wielding Gunslinger is your primary damage dealer, while the Radshot applies corrosive radiation damage, and the Nomad offers a close-range shotgun blast with knockback.

Those base-level characters offer solid variety upon which to build. And that’s where the main hook for Australia Did It comes in: experimentation through combination. In the midst of battle, you can merge two units of the same level to create new, more powerful defenders, influenced by the traits of those used in the merge. At the onset, you can merge two Nomads to create a level 2 Nomad with increased damage and knockback, but the real fun comes in combining disparate units to create completely new characters. Even now, more than 15 hours into my gameplay, I’m still concocting new combinations I want to try on my next run.

By the end of my first successful run, I had multiple level 6 characters, including a railgun-toting heavy, mages who steal health from enemies and redistribute it to nearby allies, a drone that can move beyond the walls of the station to attack enemies directly, and, my personal favorite, a dual-shotgun-wielding one-man wrecking crew. However, many of these higher-level units also possess drawbacks to consider, like the railgun scorching all adjacent tiles or the drone running out of battery if it’s outside the walls for too long. Though I started keeping notes in my head about which combinations led to my favorite results, I was grateful for a comprehensive compendium that tracked the tens of unit types I unlocked through this rewarding experimentation.

The meat of the experience places your squad on a 25-tile square board with enemies spawning from the four principal directions. Thoughtfulness and positioning are crucial, as each unit on your squad possesses different traits and movement efficiency, as do the encroaching enemies. Basic enemies often make a beeline toward the station, while others may take a weaving route or keep their distance and blast you at range. Improvising and adjusting your strategy on the fly is the most engaging part of Australia Did It, and when you perfectly adapt in the moment, or escape the scenario by the skin of your teeth, there are few better feelings I’ve experienced in a game this year.

Your goal in this phase is to simply defend the station and gather resources to strengthen your squad before evacuating and moving on to the next area. Considering each unit's strengths, weaknesses, and capabilities while strategically positioning them around the station takes some getting used to, especially during the more chaotic stages. I fist-pumped as I watched the train pull out of a station that was about to crumble, and I lamented the loss of high-level units I had to leave behind to ensure the survival of the convoy. The process is ceaselessly thrilling, even as you begin to see how the gears work under the hood. I just wish I could say the same about the intervening train sections.

Once you escape the turn-based strategy portion, your surviving squad members hop aboard the train and chart their route. Using a basic map, you choose your next stop, with factors like enemy types and modifiers shown to you ahead of time. The top-down train segments between station-defense stages are largely passive; the units you evacuated from the previous station automatically attack swarming enemies with the same traits and perks they have in the main gameplay areas. You can aim a focus cone to instruct your units, but you’re at the mercy of the units you’ve brought. You can trigger an ultimate ability to send your defenders into overdrive, but I rarely needed it.

While I love the idea of intentionally crafting a team that’s good at both the turn-based strategy and bullet-heaven transport sections, I was never fully engaged getting from point A to point B. Instead, I often caught myself checking how much longer before my train arrived at the next station; these sections can be completed in a minute or two, but that doesn’t alleviate the feeling that it’s a step down from the other gameplay. These novel portions aren’t bad by any means; they’re merely an average part of an otherwise excellent experience.

Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world.

#4076. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4074. 10 Changes You Might Not Have Noticed in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is pretty amazing. The team didn’t mess around, and instead changed many aspects of this beloved Nintendo 64 title. It has updated graphics, slightly altered story beats, and more. Of course, since the team rebuilt Hyrule, that means they could make a few changes. Castle Town is now much more detailed, and even Death Mountain’s layout changed slightly.

These are just some of the big changes, however, as Nintendo made a lot more changes, and some of them you might not even have noticed since they are so small. Despite being small, these changes are just as important as the large ones, as they make the game feel more complete.

This is a very small change that you might not have realized was made between the original game and the remake, and that is that the merchants actually move. While some of the shop owners had animation before, they typically just looked at Link.

While playing the remake, you will see that each merchant is now far more animated, but the big difference is that they will actually turn their head to look at the item you are buying from them. While this change wasn’t needed, it definitely makes the shop owners feel more alive rather than watching them stand there.

Have you ever been to Castle Town at night in the original Ocarina of Time? No? Well, that is because you can’t go there at night. The drawbridge closes, preventing you from accessing the town after sunset. Luckily, you have the Sun Song to quickly change night into day, allowing you to enter the town.

This isn’t an issue, however, in the remake, as the town is constantly open to you. You can come and go as you please at any time of the day or night without anyone getting upset with you. You may have had it in your mind to keep going during the day, or maybe you just assumed that the gate was open and forgot that it closed in the original.

Fairy Thoughts didn’t exist in the original game. Instead, they are something new that is specific to the Ocarina of Time Remake. These small glowing symbols can be found on various surfaces around Hyrule, even in dungeons. Sometimes Fairy Thoughts act as hints to help you progress through the game, and other times they are small puzzles that fully restore Link’s health once they are solved.

They are a neat little change that you might not have noticed while exploring, as they can be easy to overlook. I didn’t notice them for a long time, and since I found one, I have been going around looking for more.

Link has always been known as the silent hero of Hyrule, but the remake appears to have given him a very brief spoken line.

You may have seen various little whirlwinds around Hyrule in the remake. These are used to summon the scarecrow, and they didn’t appear in the original. In the original Ocarina of Time, if you wanted to summon Pierre, you needed to find a spot where Navi would glow green instead of the normal blue. This indicated that it was a spot where the scarecrow song could be played.

Now, if you want to summon Pierre the Wandering Scarecrow, you simply need to find a place where “the straw swirls in the wind.” Which is any location with a bit of swirling wind. At least these locations are easier to find.

There are some who received the Giant’s Knife from Goron City back in the day, swung it around to test it, and then ultimately got disappointed when it broke before they even left the area and got to test it on some enemies. For those who don’t know, this weapon is very fragile, making it so it breaks after just eight hits. It is a cautionary tale that teaches everyone that nothing is permanent, except the Master Sword.

Anyway, the weapon still breaks in the remake, but there has been a change. Nintendo removed the hitboxes from walls, so you can swing the weapon around and not have it break off the environment. Instead, it will break from striking enemies, as was intended.

The Biggoron Sword is quite powerful, and in the original game, many replaced the Master Sword with it because it could be swung at the same pace and it hit harder. The only difference was you couldn’t use your shield while wielding it. Despite that drawback, the Biggoron Sword was worth holding onto, as an experienced swordfighter didn’t need to worry about using their shield for the most part.

This sword has been changed in the remake. It is still massive, and requires both hands to swing. However, the swing speed of it is noticeably slower, making it more difficult to hit some enemies with the blade. This put more emphasis on the use of the Master Sword in certain situations.

Since The Ocarina of Time is a third-person title, you might not have realized that there was a first-person option in the original. The game did go into first-person when shooting your slingtshot, but otherwise, you needed to press a button for it, and even then it was temporary.

The remake of the beloved title doesn’t even give you the option to go into first-person mode. Instead, it keeps you tied to the third-person camera. This is a bit of a strange change from the original and one that some people discovered right away, as they used to use first-person mode to get a closer look at the environment. To replace it, many have said that Nintendo should have added a photo mode.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has finally been released, and fans have already discovered several game-breaking glitches.

One of the side quests you can complete in Ocarina of Time is the one for the Happy Mask Salesman. This quest requires you to purchase various masks and sell them to citizens of Hyrule. However, in the original, you weren’t allowed to wear the masks as an adult. People always thought this was a bit strange, but it is a detail that didn’t matter much.

The remake, on the other hand, allows you to wear the various masks as an adult. There isn’t anything special about wearing the masks as an adult versus wearing them as a kid, but it is an interesting little detail that Nintendo added that wasn’t in the original game.

After progressing through the game, you finally make your way to the Spirit Temple. This is one of my personal favorite temples in the game, and like the other temples in the game, it has undergone some changes in the remake.

One of the more peculiar changes is the one made to the large Gerudo statue in the temple. In the original, certain parts of the statue were able to be grappled using your hookshot, but there were never any obvious grapple points. This has been changed in the remake, with the statue still being there, but the grapple points are now gone, so you can no longer grab the statue if it’s something that interests you.

This is a bit of an odd change, but one that people are thankful has been made. In the original Ocarina of Time, when you reach the Zora’s Domain, you talk to King Zora, and you eventually get him to scoot out of the way so you can visit Lord Jabu-Jabu. This scoot is obnoxiously long, as King Zora likes to take his time getting out of your way.

Well, in the remake, King Zora still scoots out of the way, but the change is that Nintendo made is significantly quicker. When timed, King Zora moves out of the way roughly eight seconds faster than he does in the original Ocarina of Time. Thankfully, we only need to wait around 20 seconds now instead of almost 30. Nintendo kept this hilarious if frustrating part of the title in, but streamlined it considerably.

Some of the original's most charming quirks from Zelda: Ocarina of Time didn't make the journey.

#4073. MTG Star Trek Card Featuring Patrick Stewart Sells At $26K

Magic: The Gathering isn't exactly a stranger when it comes to ridiculously expensive cards, and while resellers aren't quite as rabid as some other TCGs, even somewhat less popular sets like Star Trek are still reaching hefty prices on the second-hand market. While the price might not compete with Lord of the Rings' over $2M One Ring card, getting one of MTG's new serialized cards will still cost you quite a bit.

While the seven hand-signed card variants introduced in MTG's Star Trek Collector's Boosters were already going to be a massive hit due to their limited availability, one of them has already broken the $20,000 mark, albeit for a bit of a morbid reason.

As shared by moombahh on Reddit, while most autographed Star Trek cards go for around $5-10K USD, a recent eBay listing for none other than Captain Jean-Luc Picard reportedly sold for a whopping $26K. While it's entirely possible the buyer sent a lower offer, it might even end up on the cheaper side of the spectrum if the other eBay listings are anything to go by.

With more recent listings having shot up all the way to $38K and an even more massive $45K, the price could wind up being well above the last sold price, and it's not hard to see why either.

For the first time ever, you can pack signed MTG cards, with seven to collect in total, but the first two revealed are of Captains Kirk and Janeway.

Dwarfing the Secret Lair card prices, the main reason players have been pricing their cards so high is that, since signing the cards, Jean-Luc Picard's actor, Patrick Stewart, recently passed away, leaving the serialized cards among the last items signed by the legendary actor.

While fans have pointed out that it's more than a little depressing that others are trying to capitalize on the late actor's passing by selling the cards for absurd prices, it's unlikely that sellers will be slowing down anytime soon, considering how limited their availability will continue to be.

Among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

#4071. Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment

Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening.

Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations.

Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

#4070. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4069. Take-Two CEO Outlines Conditions for a GTA Show or Film

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

Arguably, one of the main elements that gives the Grand Theft Auto series its powerful, widespread appeal is its congruity with modern film and television. It’s an extremely cinematic series, both in and out of actual gameplay, with a particular emphasis on building strong narratives and compelling characters. Given all of that, the idea of pursuing a live-action adaptation of the series, either in the form of a television series or a feature film, seems kind of obvious.

With the looming release of Grand Theft Auto 6 and the immeasurable hype it’s brought with it, not to mention the recent success of video game adaptations in both film and TV like the live-action Fallout series or the new season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, it might just be a perfect time to start shopping the GTA IP around for other media avenues.

In an interview with The David Rubenstein Show podcast, relayed via Deadline, Take-Two Interactive’s CEO, Strauss Zelnick, admitted that the idea has naturally crossed his and his company’s collective minds, and the chance is definitely not zero. However, if it were to happen, it could only happen in a very particular circumstance.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

In the interview, Zelnick was asked how he felt about “line extensions” in regard to the GTA IP. In other words, branches out into other forms of media and licensing beyond just video games, which would naturally include television and film.

“We’re very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth – entertainment we’re always proud of,” Zelnick responded.

Zelnick explained that Take-Two and Rockstar could absolutely head up a live-action adaptation of GTA, either a specific game or the franchise as a whole, but he’d only be willing to give it the green light if absolutely everyone involved were completely and totally committed and confident.

We’re very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth.

If the creative teams weren’t just confident that a hypothetical movie or show would be well-liked by viewers, but willing to tackle the task with genuine, uncompromising passion, it simply wouldn’t meet his standards.

“It’s a high bar to do that, and of course, there’s always a risk of failure. So we don’t rule it out, but we’re very, very selective,” Zelnick cautioned.

I don’t think it’d be hyperbolic to say that Take-Two Interactive and Rockstar Games are about to make a lot of money, to put it very mildly. The world is spinning on the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and with pre-order profits through the roof and critics already singing praises, this game is slated to become one of the definitive faces of the gaming industry and a tentpole of current pop culture besides.

All of that is to say that, given recent trends in the broader entertainment sphere, I have a feeling a lot of doors are about to open to GTA as an IP. Not that they were previously closed per se, as the series’ previous games were all exceptionally popular and profitable. Rather, the sphere seems a lot more willing to jump on gaming bandwagons than it was even a decade ago, and if GTA 6 pulls the kinds of numbers it’s projected to, the proverbial phone is going to be ringing off the hook with offers and deals.

We’re probably not going to see a GTA show or movie in the immediate future, but with the cash and resources Take-Two will undoubtedly accrue from this release, it could manifest sooner than we expect.

#4068. PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio

PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.

The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.

"While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop.

Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs.

The votes have been cast and the nominees for 2026's Game of the Year have been revealed. Six of the past year's biggest and best games, and as always, the games that have and haven't made the cut are being hotly debated. There's also a remake in the mix this year along with a game that hadn't been released when the nominations were announced, so a lot for those who think the awards should have clearer criteria to discuss.

Whether you agree with all six nominees or not, it's hard to argue that the games in the running this year aren't six of the six biggest games released this calendar year. The games that, if you haven't played anything else this year, or if there are some you missed, you should probably try your best to play before we get to 2027 and another year of new games begins. Whether you're wondering whether you have the right hardware before buying the nominees, want to know if they have a physical release, or you just want to know how much they cost, you'll find everything you need to know to fill in your GOTY gaps below.

GTA 6 is finally here, and its Game of the Year nomination has caused a stir. The game will be here by the time the awards are handed out, but it was nominated two days before release. That doesn't matter to you right now, though. The launch of GTA 6 is mere hours away as I type this, and if you're not one of the 15 million people who have placed a pre-order, here's what you need to know.

As long as you ignore the state of rent, wages, and world economics, GTA 6's price tag isn't that bad, you guys!

GTA 6 will only be available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S when released. Its PC launch will follow at a later, still unrevealed, time. There are two editions to choose from - standard and ultimate. The standard edition will provide tens, if not hundreds, of hours of entertainment, but there will be various stores, barbers, and tattoo parlors that are off-limits if you don't own the ultimate edition.

The standard edition of GTA 6 is $79.99 on both PS5 and Series X|S, while the ultimate edition is $99.99 on both platforms.

GTA 6 isn't the only game that has caused a stir by picking up a GOTY nomination this year. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has poked the beehive that is remakes being eligible to win the prestigious award. If there was ever a remake that was going to qualify, it's a universally loved one like this that somehow reimagines one of the greatest games of all time without upsetting any of the original's fans.

There is only one place you can play the Ocarina of Time remake, and that's on Switch 2. There are no different editions to choose from, but there is a physical release, and since this is a Switch 2 exclusive, there's a price difference between its digital and physical versions. A digital copy of Ocarina of Time costs $59.99, but if you want a physical copy, it'll cost you $69.99.

Robert Pattinson might be the next James Bond on the big screen, but Patrick Gibson became the video game Bond this year in the critically acclaimed 007 First Light. A performance so good that not only were fans suggesting Gibson could potentially make the jump to Bond movies, but the odds of that happening spiked significantly after the game was released.

First Light is the first nominee on the list that's available to play on Steam. It's also on PS5 and Series X|S, and while a Switch 2 version was promised, it has been delayed until March 18, 2027. I have played a little bit of the game on Switch 2, and for what it's worth, I didn't encounter any issues and was a little surprised that its release was moved into 2027.

It's amazing to see just how far this series has come since the low point that was Resident Evil 6. The trilogy that has followed, alongside the remakes of games from its heyday, has put Resident Evil firmly back on top of the video game mountain. That's why Resident Evil Requiem, a game many would describe as the best new Resi game in decades, is in the running to be crowned Game of the Year.

If you're trying to play all of these games before a winner is crowned, or you want to get one under your belt quickly, Requiem is the place to start. By far the shortest nominee on this year's GOTY list, with a story that takes around 11 hours to play through according to How Long To Beat. It's also the only one of all six nominees that's available on all major platforms, with those who played on Switch 2 awarding it, and Capcom's other day-one Switch 2 releases this year, high praise.

Phantom Blade Zero is a game people have been waiting a long time for. Shown off for the first time well over three years ago, S-Game's action-packed epic finally arrived in October, and it did not disappoint. Rave reviews and a player base that wholeheartedly agrees with what the critics had to say about it have landed it among 2026's Game of the Year nominees.

Your platform options are limited for this one - just PS5 for console players, but it is on PC too if you prefer to play there. There's no physical release either, which is unfortunate, although a physical edition of the PS5 version has been promised for 2027. Hopefully there aren't any issues getting that out on time, with PlayStation pushing forward with its promise to stop putting games on discs in 2028.

Control Resonant might be the most surprising inclusion among this year's Game of the Year nominees. Not because it doesn't deserve to be on this list, but because it's the only game of the six where the combined reaction to its release wasn't overwhelmingly positive, unlike the other five. Not that many people had anything negative to say about it, just that it didn't seem to blow everyone away quite as much as its GOTY competitors.

Now that said, if you want to play the best games 2026 has to offer, Control Resonant should unquestionably be on your list, particularly if you liked the first game and you're an Alan Wake fan. It's available on PS5, Xbox, and PC, there's a physical version if you're into that kind of thing, and it's slightly more expensive and includes an extra outfit, resources, and a digital artbook and soundtrack.

Steam has incredible sales all year round, but nothing quite compares to the deals you can get during the holiday season!

#4066. GDC Survey Suggests Devs Want To Make Games For Switch 2 More Than PS5 Or Xbox

The GDC Festival of Gaming has published its latest 'State of the Game Industry' report, which is based on a survey of over 2,600 game industry professionals on topics such as AI, layoffs, labour, and more.

One particular result caught our eye, and it's regarding which platforms developers are currently interested in developing for in the future. As expected, PC was comfortably the winner at 81%, likely down to its versatility, ease-of-use, and broad visibility of storefronts like Steam and Epic Games Store.

However, it's the Switch 2 that bagged the silver medal at 46%, putting it ahead of the PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Steam Deck, Steam Machine, and even upcoming consoles like the PS6 and Project Helix.

Since its release in June 2025, the Switch 2 has seen a staggering number of releases, from high-profile 'AAA' titles to smaller indie games, and it seems this is only set to continue or perhaps even accelerate in the future.

In a similar chart looking at which platform(s) developers' upcoming game or project will ship on next, the Switch 2 ranks lower than PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Steam Deck, pulling in 29% of the vote. With this one, however, it's worth considering external factors that might be at play.

For example, it's easy to say that you want to develop for the Switch 2, but whether you have the budget and dev kits to actually do so is another question. Just something to consider when looking at these results.
