#4065. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4064. GTA 6 Just Broke Twitch's Biggest Viewership Record In Just 30 Minutes

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

If you thought the hype surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 couldn't possibly get any bigger, the game's launch has already found a way to prove you wrong! After becoming one of the highest-rated games ever, more impressive numbers are popping up.

While most players are still waiting for November 19 to arrive (less than 24 hours now, folks!), fans in regions like New Zealand have already gotten their hands on Rockstar's long-awaited open-world adventure. And it took just minutes for the game to make streaming history.

According to data from Streams Charts, GTA 6 already attracted more than 5.3 million concurrent viewers across major livestreaming platforms shortly after becoming available in New Zealand. That figure was already enough to smash the previous record for a video game launch, and the numbers have continued climbing as the release rolls out to more countries.

By the time the game became available in Japan and South Korea, its combined audience had reached an astonishing 7.18 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick. And that's before every other region has even had a chance to jump into Vice City!

Sam Houser offered up a rare statement ahead of what might just be the biggest video game launch in modern history.

To put things in a broader perspective, the previous record for the biggest video game launch in streaming history belonged to Valorant. Riot Games' shooter attracted approximately 1.74 million concurrent viewers during its closed beta in April 2020, a number that seemed almost impossible to beat at the time.

Well, GTA 6 has more than quadrupled that figure. According to Streams Charts' preliminary data, the game currently leads its ranking of the biggest game launches by Peak Viewers with 7,183,979 concurrent viewers. Hogwarts Legacy follows in third place with approximately 1.36 million, while Path of Exile 2 and Lost Ark round out the top five.

By the time the game became available in Japan and South Korea, its combined audience had reached an astonishing 7.18 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick.

The numbers are particularly impressive considering that the game's worldwide release is still underway. As more players gain access, additional streamers are expected to go live, potentially pushing the record even higher!

It is also worth looking at how the audience is distributed across platforms. Twitch currently leads with a peak of 3.06 million viewers, followed by YouTube with 2.74 million and Kick with 1.36 million. Twitch's figure makes GTA 6 the second-most-watched gaming category in the platform's history, narrowly behind League of Legends and its 3.11 million peak.

12.5 million American gamers plan to adjust their schedules for Rockstar's next big release.

Besides, the game's launch has also been an important moment for individual creators. Streams Charts reports that HoneyMad currently leads the list of streamers with the highest concurrent audiences, reaching 576,313 viewers on Twitch. And Brazilian streamer alanzoka also had a huge launch, setting a new personal record with 313,548 live viewers.

And to be completely honest, it is hard to imagine anyone being particularly surprised by these numbers! GTA 5 has remained one of the biggest games on streaming platforms for more than a decade, and its successor has arrived with an unprecedented level of anticipation.

Of course, it is important to remember that these figures are still preliminary. Streams Charts notes that its latest data was collected at 12:30 UTC on November 18, and the numbers are expected to change as the game becomes available in more regions. Still, GTA 6 has already accomplished something no other game launch has managed before. If this is what the first few hours look like, I can't wait to see what happens once everyone can finally play.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4063. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4062. Lego And TT Games Seemingly Tease A New Lego James Bond Game

The Lego games have been a part of many gamers' childhoods, but TT Games has more than proven in recent years that their family-friendly gaming adaptations can be enjoyed by just about anyone regardless of their age. While rumors have been circulating about what the next Lego gaming project would be after it was leaked to be a Warner Bros. property, some recent teases have fans thinking otherwise.

While it's far from an official confirmation of any kind, both TT Games and Lego themselves chiming in on the topic already has fans fully convinced that a previously cancelled Lego game could be getting the modern-day return it desperately deserves.

First spotted by CrazyLegoMoment on X, a suspicious series of tweets was made after it was announced Robert Pattinson would be taking the mantle of James Bond moving forward, starting with TT Games responding with a pair of eyes emoji when Shai Matheson (voice of Batman in Lego Batman: Legacy of The Dark Knight) joked that he would be "the next Lego Bond".

As if that wasn't enough, even the official Lego account responded by saying "he's got a license to build" when another fan posted about wanting an official Lego James Bond game made by TT Games.

Legacy of the Dark Knight has clocked up impressive enough review scores to make it the highest-rated Lego game ever.

While these could certainly just be some members of the studios trying to join in on the viral sensation and memes coming out of the news, an official announcement wouldn't be much of a surprise considering TT Games had already pitched several James Bond-themed Lego games in the past, one of which saw its entire pitch trailer leaked last year to the excitement of countless fans.

Having supposedly rejected TT Games' take on Bond for the subject material being "too mature" for the Lego in the past, the company has since branched out to countless adult franchises for official sets and even triple-A games like Legacy of The Dark Knight that Bond would feel right at home with for a full-blown adaptation.

Combined with the unique gameplay mechanics, open-world, and sheer level of detail offered by TT Games' previous Legacy of the Dark Knight and Skywalker Saga, a standalone Lego James Bond game would be a perfect fit with countless vehicles, gadgets, and costumes to experiment with.

With 27 films over the past 60 years to pull from, a Lego James Bond game isn't exactly starved for potential when it comes to levels and characters either, which would also offer the perfect tie-in game for whenever Robert Pattinson's upcoming Bond film releases.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4061. The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Is Nintendo's Fastest-Selling Switch 2 Game Ever

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo's second remake of the original N64 game that first launched way back in 1998, is the fastest-selling Nintendo-published game on the Switch 2 ever. That accolade comes after the game sold more than 5.2 million copies in just four days following its November 5 launch last week.

This remake is already the Switch 2's second-best-selling Nintendo game at 5.2 million units sold, behind Mario Kart World's impressive 16.48 million copies sold to date. If The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time keeps this pace up, it could one day overtake Mario Kart World, though the Mario Kart series typically holds onto that top spot. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is still far and away the best-selling game on Switch.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the crown jewel of Nintendo's 40th Zelda series anniversary celebration, which also includes other games, products, and even an upcoming worldwide orchestral tour. Plus, a live-action Legend of Zelda film will debut in theaters worldwide on April 30, 2027.

Game Informer gave The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a 9.25 out of 10 in its review, with our reviewer Kyle Hilliard writing, "For many like me, the original Ocarina of Time is an impactful adventure that arrived at a time in their lives when magic still felt real. Playing the game 28 years later and appreciating the care taken to maintain and improve the original vision was the ultimate surprise of the whole experience: I didn't expect to be so moved."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched last week exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

For more, read this interview with the remake's producers about changes to the original game, easter eggs, the Bombchu bowling alley operator, and more, then check out this feature breaking down the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time easter eggs that did and didn't make it into this 2026 remake. After that, read about how the Switch 2 Pro controller can make The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time even better, then check out this interview with award-winning composer and musician Jon Batiste about the Ocarina of Time score.

Did you pick up The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time last week? Let us know what you think of it so far in the comments below!

#4060. "Pressure To Go For The Cheaper Option Grows" - XSEED Reckons Game-Key Cards Are Here To Stay

"The end of physical media was declared many years ago"

Amongst the Switch 2's many Game-Key Card physical releases in its first year, Marvelous USA/XSEED has stood firm as one of the few third-party publishers consistently offering complete-on-card releases. Nintendo's new smaller cart option may entice more studios to follow suit, but XSEED CEO Ken Berry can't see the format going away any time soon.

In a new RPG Site interview all about the state of physical media in 2026, Berry admitted that it's actually "getting harder" for publishers to bring 'proper' physical releases to Switch 2, as GKCs are "getting more and more accepted," leading to a growing "pressure to go for the cheaper option".

He continues that despite smaller cart options coming into play, there's still a hefty amount of uncertainty when it comes to component pricing:

Future uncertainty on pricing on anything that contains computer chips due to what’s affectionately called the ongoing RAMpocalypse would point to disc-based or Game-Key Card releases as maybe having even a greater cost advantage in the future.

It's not something that Marvelous/XSEED is using itself, mind you. The publisher released proper physical editions for Rune Factory: Guardians of Azuma, Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar and Daemon x Machina: Titanic Scion in North America last year, and is continuing that with Muramasa: Revenant Blades, Fate/Extra Record and Eternal Anima in 2027 (some of which will receive a GKC release in other regions).

"The end of physical media was declared many years ago, but we continued to see strong demand for them, especially the premium SKUs such as limited editions," Barry says. "But I would say in the past year or two it has really shifted where, after the initial shipment of units goes out at launch, even if it sells through to the end consumers really well, we don’t get the kind of reorders from retailers to restock their inventory the way we used to."

By the sound of things, Barry seems convinced to keep the physical releases going for as long as possible in North America — he notes that things can be more "challenging" in the EU thanks to "All the different countries and languages they have to accommodate". And long may it continue!

While Nintendo apparently has its smaller 32GB cards now available, it'll take continued appetite for full on-cart releases to convince publishers that they are worthwhile.

#4059. 8 Mistakes Everyone Made When Playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Many of us grew up with the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and were excited when The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake was announced. We had years upon years to play the original title, and it has honed our skills for the remake.

Of course, that is what everyone thought, and then when each of us started the remake we all started making numerous mistakes. Maybe you completely forgot about the sprint button, or maybe you completely forgot that you can manually jump now.

There are a bunch of mistakes that are easy to make when you have the muscle memory of the original game baked into your being.

The original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is known for not having a dedicated jump button. Actually many of the early Zelda titles didn’t have a dedicated jump button. Of course, this was changed in the remake, and Nintendo made sure that everyone was aware of that.

When the remake was finally shown off, Nintendo made sure to emphasize that you could manually jump instead of relying on hitting a ledge. Despite this, I know I am not the only one who walked off a ledge.

Even though Nintendo told everyone about the jump button, we all ran to a ledge and muscle memory took over, so instead of jumping, we all just fell off into the water around Kokiri Forest.

Autosave has been around in games for a long time, but it didn’t always exist. Back in the day, you needed to manually save all of your games or you lost your data when things went south.

I know multiple people who gave up playing Ocarina of Time for a bit because they forgot to save. Now, you don’t need to worry about it, as there is an autosave feature in the remake.

I can’t be the only one who relied entirely on the autosave. In fact, I didn’t manually save for the first few hours of playing the game, and it came back to bite me later on. Make sure you always save your game and don’t just assume the autosave has your back.

Zelda Notes statistics reveal that the most common causes of death are surprisingly embarrassing.

There are some classic Rupee exploits we used to perform in the original Ocarina of Time, with one of the most obvious being the drawbridge jump. When you climbed the chains attached to the drawbridge, you could make some easy money by jumping off along the wall.

This would get you red Rupees, which are worth 20 Rupees, and that went a long way towards purchasing some important items. However, these exploits don’t work anymore.

The remake has removed the exploits from days past, and now we must rely on new exploits to gather a bunch of Rupees in a quick manner, but that doesn’t mean we all didn’t try it anyway.

After we beat the original Ocarina of Time, it became a habit to want to beat it as fast as possible, and thus, the insane number of speedrun attempts started, making Ocarina of Time one of the most replayed games in history.

If you were someone who tried to speedrun the game over and over again, you might have tried to perform one of the speedrunning tactics only to find that they just don’t work anymore. Nintendo didn’t even purposefully leave any in as a tribute.

However, that hasn’t stopped gamers from figuring out many of the remake’s glitches. Now you can skip straight to the Shadow Temple after leaving Kokiri Forest.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has finally been released, and fans have already discovered several game-breaking glitches.

After you play through a game enough, you remember the various details, like where a key is supposed to be, or the layout of a dungeon. There are many people who remember the layouts of every dungeon in Ocarina of Time like the back of their hand.

All this muscle memory doesn’t help in the remake, as the dungeons have been redesigned. Some of the rooms are different, and there are even some new areas to explore that weren’t in the original.

It has made the remake feel like a brand new Zelda title rather than the same old game everyone is used to, but the fact remains that you probably thought a room would be in a specific place and ended up running into a wall.

Redeads were terrifying when in the original Ocarina of Time. Their lifeless bodies freaked out many kids back in the day, and Nintendo managed to keep that same feeling alive in the remake.

Many people, like myself, underestimated the newer version of the Redeads. Nintendo made them much quicker this time around, and it is very easy to get caught in their screams.

I went into the game thinking I would easily take them down, and I do now, but at first, I was grabbed, and it took me off guard. They are much more menacing this time around and shouldn’t be taken lightly.

Motion controls can be the bane of anyone’s existence if they aren’t prepared for them. Back in the day, Nintendo didn’t have motion controls in games, meaning those who grew up with the original Ocarina of Time didn’t need to worry about them.

However, since the Nintendo Switch 2 has motion controls, Nintendo decided to turn them on for the start of the Ocarina of Time Remake. If you didn’t know this, it became very apparent when playing the slingshot mini-game.

As soon as I started the mini-game, something felt off, and I quickly noticed that my aim was being controlled by my movement. I am not the only one who didn’t realize motion controls were automatically turned on, and we all quickly turned them off.

Remember, if you want to use your slingshot, you need to be a kid. If you want to use your bow, you need to be an adult. This is a very common mistake that was made in the original, and now it is common to make in the remake.

Child Link and adult Link have two different inventories. Some items that work for you as a kid, don’t work when you are an adult and vice-versa. This can be a bit annoying, especially since an adult definitely knows how to use a boomerang.

Anyway, it is a mistake that we have all made, as it is easy to play as one version of Link for a while, switch to the other version, and then forget what items you have access to.

Some of the original's most charming quirks from Zelda: Ocarina of Time didn't make the journey.

#4058. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

#4057. Marvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Reportedly Still In Development Amid Rumors Of Its Cancellation

Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

However, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no announced platforms.

Although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

#4056. Helldivers 2 Devs Say Bouncy Stratagem Fix Is Still “In Development”

Helldivers 2 has had a rollercoaster of fan reactions since its release, flipping between one of the most hyped PvE games in recent years and an incredibly controversial sci-fi shooter. While much of this criticism springs from just how popular and surprising the success story behind Helldivers 2 is compared to its predecessor, Arrowhead Studios still seems to be working on issues that have been plaguing the game since release.

This isn't to say that fans have been starving for content, with a whole new faction, numerous collaborations, and plenty of live-service events to keep them busy, but even dedicated members of the community are feeling frustrated by just how long it took for Helldivers 2's upcoming gameplay change.

If you've ever played Helldivers 2 before, you'll definitely have encountered the problem of throwing down a Stratagem on a rocky surface, or even a flat building, before it winds up bouncing dozens of meters away from where you intended.

While you might have assumed this was an intended feature to limit their effectiveness, Arrowhead Studios themselves have revealed it's actually a bug on X that they're actively working to fix.

Rather than being happy about the change, fans have been using it as a point of criticism over wondering how they are expected to be "hyped over a bug fix that should've happened in 2024," alongside other players noting that "modders fixed this and hellpod steering long ago."

As if that wasn't enough, the long-awaited bug fix is not even being added to the game yet, with "more information coming in the new year" to the disappointment of many players.

While it's still certainly great to see Helldivers still getting updates and quality of life fixes years after release, it's not hard to see why players are so frustrated either, especially after the implementation of stricter anti-cheat that ended up disabling countless fan-made mods.

#4055. The Sims 4 patch makes it so your public lot gatherings won't be interrupted by rogue Sims

Stranger Sims will no longer just crash your public lot events in The Sims 4 to talk about whatever.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

#4054. GTA 6: Where to Find Strip Clubs

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

Who doesn’t like to party a little in games? Well, Grand Theft Auto 6 certainly has various means to do so. Whether it’s a club, a fancy VIP experience, or a traditional strip club, Vice City has everything you’re looking for.

This has been a staple of the series ever since Grand Theft Auto 3, as going into these clubs not only facilitated story missions but also allowed the characters (and the player) to get an NSFW experience. There are a handful of different options in Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto 6, but finding them can be a bit tricky. Most of them are centralized, and some you won’t see until much later in the campaign.

Players already have a list of 61 cheats to look forward to.

The first strip club you’ll find is in Chapter 2 upon meeting Vicki who will introduce you to her boss at the Delights Cabaret. This is a traditional strip club, but one that’s more in line with being out in the middle of nowhere. It’s more of a bar atmosphere with girls in the back.

With that said, you’ll be able to find Delights Cabaret in the Port Gellhorn section of the map, all the way to the west.

The first strip club you’ll come across in Vice City is part of the story between Jason and his old buddy Dre’Quan. He will invite you out to his club, where he will introduce you to Boobie, who will be putting Jason and Lucia up in his apartment.

This is a traditional strip club, with dancers on poles. It’s also one of the more expensive clubs, with VIP dance treatments costing $1,000. Jack of Hearts is located in central Crosstown, just south of your apartment. This is the go-to spot for adult entertainment.

This has more of a club vibe with a bit of stripping. It’s far fancier than Jack of Hearts, but has just as many options, if not more, with dancing on the dancefloor. The best part is that the VIP dances will only set you back $300 in-game.

NINE1NINE is south of Jack of Hearts, at the top of the Downtown section of the map. Even when you roll up to the place for the first time, you’ll notice just how much nicer it is, with a more exclusive feeling.

This is less of a strip club and more of a dance club. At least one main mission takes place here, and it’s probably the best place to go dancing with Lucia. It features multiple rooms with different types of music and DJs, and its aesthetic is built around an old vault, with a giant vault door at the entrance.

It’s definitely somewhere to check out in Vice City, and thankfully, it’s right across the street from NINE1NINE, just to the west.

Last but not least is VYB. It’s located in the northeast portion of Ocean Beach, directly south of your Act 4 home in Washington Beach. Similar to The Vault, it has a more traditional club atmosphere, with dance floors and high-class bars in the back.

Unfortunately, VYB isn’t accessible to the public, as it’s part of Dre’Quan’s lengthy story and is only used during a main mission in Act 4. With that said, it’s probably the nicest club in the game.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4052. Civilization Developer Firaxis Games Cuts A Third Of Its Staff, Studio Head Departs

A new report from Bloomberg reveals that Firaxis Games, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, has cut around one third of its staff. Meanwhile, its studio head Heather Hazen will also depart.

Approximately 60 people have been laid off as work on a new XCOM stalled over the Summer, with the game reportedly missing a huge milestone. Development will continue, but it will likely be met with a pretty drastic shake-up.

A spokesperson for 2K, a subsidiary of Take-Two, shared the following statement:

“Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength — designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis.

"These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

Funny how they try to spin these statements to make it sound almost positive, eh?

Firaxis most recently released Civilization VII for the Switch and Switch 2, amongst other major platforms. Reception was fairly mixed, but it received a solid 8/10 from us upon its release on the Switch 1. Since then, it's received numerous updates, but it's arguably failed to achieve the same success as earlier entries.

It's particularly egregious that this should come just a couple of days before the release of GTA 6, another Take-Two title developed by Rockstar Games. It's set to be one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time, but it seems Take-Two felt the need to save even more money elsewhere.

#4050. Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

Finally, a PC specification list that actually indicates resolution and framerate targets, and doesn't leave console players behind.

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

#4049. God Of War Sons Of Sparta Gets PS4 Version And New Content Next Monday

It's been about nine months since Sony Santa Monica and Mega Cat Studios dropped God of War Sons of Sparta as a surprise reveal and launch during a State of Play. If you haven't checked it out yet, the developers are giving you some new reasons to today, unveiling two new modes and a new platform: PlayStation 4.

If you don't remember, God of War Sons of Sparta is a prequel spin-off of the God of War series, showing protagonist Kratos as a 13-year-old soldier, long before his god-killing days. The game features 2D combat and a Metroidvania-style map, along with a fully voiced cast of characters including Scott Menville (who you might recognize as Robin in Teen Titans) as Kratos' brother Deimos, Jack Quaid (who will voice a different character in God of War Laufey next year), and TC Carson, who returns from the original trilogy as the voice of adult Kratos.

Announced in a post on the PlayStation Blog today, Sons of Sparta is making the jump back to Sony's previous console, which is now (brace yourself) 13 years old. Sons of Sparta's 2D pixel art is far less demanding than the other God of War entries, though, so it's no surprise this was possible – it's mainly surprising that they're doing it at all.

For PS5 players who already own the game, developer Mega Cat is also adding two new modes: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode. Hermes Mode, named after the Greek god of wind, mail, and speed, is a speedrun mode that encourages you to beat the game as quickly as possible, complete with a split-based timer in the upper right-hand corner of the screen. Meanwhile, Erebus Mode, named after one of the domains of the underworld (you'll be familiar with it if you've played the Hades games), makes the game far deadlier as Kratos and all his foes die in a single hit. You'll have to wait until you beat the game once to unlock Erebus Mode, but you can access Hermes Mode from a fresh save by entering the following (and semi-familiar) code in the start menu: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad.

The free update and PS4 version will be available next Monday, November 16, at midnight local time. For more Sons of Sparta, check out our review. For more God of War, bad news: God of War Laufey was just delayed until May.

#4047. A Complete Guide To The Dune My Arrakis, My Superdrop Secret Lair MTG Drop

This new sci-fi Secret Lair contains three drops in total, but will have a slightly different format due to the availability of nonfoil cards.

We're gearing up for another Magic: The Gathering Secret Lair drop, and this time it's Dune-themed to celebrate the recent trilogy's conclusion.

Three bundles are coming to the Secret Lair at the end of the month, and there are some changes being made to the options on offer, specifically in relation to the foiling options that are available, alongside the absence of some nonfoil bundles, too. It's not clear if this is anything to do with the ongoing availability issues, but in some cases, nonfoil bundles are due to be available at WPN game stores "at a later date."

The My Arrakis, My Superdrop Secret Lair is launching on Monday, November 30, 2026 at 9 am PT (12 pm ET, 5 pm GMT, 6 pm CET). This is scheduled to be a normal Secret Lair drop, meaning the waiting room will be open from one hour before the sale time, and you can put any products you wish to buy into a basket ready to check out once you make it through the queue.

As for prices, the Desert of Arrakis and Balance of Power bundles both cost $39.99 for the nonfoil variants and $49.99 for the foil alternative. With the Spice drop, it is only available in Halo Foil, and will cost $59.99.

Finally, the promo card for this superdrop is Emperor's Hutment, which is a reskinned and renamed Reliquary Tower. You get a copy of this card for each $149.99 spent on an order.

This bundle contains five card and a token. Three of the cards a renamed reprints, one is just an art swap, and one is a brand new to Magic card.

Shai-Hulud is the new-to-Magic card and is a nine-mana green 12/12 creature with Trample and Indestructible. When it enters, you destroy all artifacts and enchantments. For each player who controller a permanent destroyed this way, search your library for a basic land card or a Desert card. Put those cards onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

It's an immensely powerful card that comes with a huge cost attached to it. But even at nine-mana with three green pips, you can ramp up to this card soon enough in the right deck. However, holding onto a card like this until the right moment will be key, as you want to make sure you're disrupting everyone's boards as much as possible by taking out valuable artifacts and enchantments.

The rumors were true and a Magic: The Gathering x Dune Secret Lair Superdrop is coming later this month.

This bundle contains eight cards, all of which are new-to-Magic.

This is an immensely exciting bundle, especially for fans of Dune, but even for general Magic fans, some of these potential Commanders are looking very interesting to build around.

The final bundle from this superdrop contains six cards, four of which are renamed reprints, one is just a reprint with fresh art, and the final card is a token.

Most notable here is a reprint of Darksteel Forge, a $40+ card, but we don't expect the value of other printings to be impacted by this release too much given that it has been renamed and comes with Dune-themed art. Secret Lair cards can sometimes help lower rare card prices, but when they're a Universes Beyond release, the market tends not to react.

#4046. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

#4045. Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns Of The Patriots: Part 8 – A Nostalgic Island Getaway | Super Replay

In 2008, Kojima Productions released what was billed as the swan song for Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear series: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots. The game had the staggering task of tying up decades of storytelling by bringing together Solid Snake, Ocelot, Otacon, Raiden, and many more characters for one explosive finale. The adventure centers on a rapidly aging Solid Snake racing against the clock to stop his twin and nemesis, Liquid Snake, one last time. Of course, there are far more bizarre shenanigans at play.

Guns of the Patriots was acclaimed for its storytelling, cinematic presentation, and evolution of the series' stealth gameplay, namely the OctoCamo suit that allowed Snake to mimic the appearance/texture of any surface he touched. It also has the distinct honor of earning a rare 10/10 review score from Game Informer. Now, thanks to the Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2, we can finally revisit MGS 4 without dusting off a PlayStation 3.

Join recent Metal Gear convert Charles Harte, who will be on the sticks to experience Guns of the Patriots (via the Master Collection Vol. 2) for the very first time, alongside long-time series fan Marcus Stewart, who is revisiting MGS 4 for the first time in over a decade. The stream kicks off today live on Twitch and YouTube at 12 p.m. PT/3 p.m. ET, and will continue for two hours each week until we roll credits.

If you can't catch us live, you can watch each episode after they air by following the YouTube links below.

Every week, Game Informer editors enter the vault and dust off games from every genre and platform imaginable. Watch Replay to relive fond (and not so fond) memories from gaming’s past.

#4044. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 13, 2026

Today is Friday the 13th, but let's not dwell on that. Here are some weekend video games to play. Well, actually, here are some of our biggest stories of the week, and then you can check out some weekend game recommendations.

Also, go ahead and make some space on your Xbox or PlayStation hard drive to make room for GTAVI. It's going to be about 200 GB and you can pre-load it now. Delete those games you're not going to return to. Delete all those video clips you'll never watch from every time you get a Trophy on your PlayStation. And you know what? Go ahead and delete Fortnite, too. It's time.

Calling all sickos of The Rootrees Are Dead, Return of the Obra Dinn, The Incident At Galley House, and everything in between: there’s another good deduction game to obsess over. Funeral for the Sun stars a historian who visits an abandoned Latin American town to piece together its turbulent history, chiefly the truth behind the mysterious disappearance of its hundreds of residents (who were, officially speaking, lost in a fire). Supernatural forces allow players to peer into the town’s past to learn about key people potentially responsible for the calamity, who they must identify by name, establish relationships between, and even match younger and older versions of themselves. You even keep track of information using a multi-function notebook à la The Roottrees Are Dead. Boasting an enticing story, a beautiful painterly art direction, and a tight runtime at roughly 8-hours (or less if you’re really on a roll), Funeral for the Sun is a mystery worth unraveling if you need a new deduction game to cozy up with.

NetEase has continued to impress with the pace and quality of its regular updates to Marvel Rivals, which continues today with the release of an 11th season for the superhero battler. Right here at launch, the notable addition is he arrival of X-Men hero Nightcrawler, who BAMFs his way into battle as a strategist, equally capable of healing allies and taking out foes with his sword and brimstone bombs. As is almost always the case right at a new hero’s launch, it can be hard to snag him on the roster on opening day to see how he plays, but once you do, I expect you’ll find him a versatile healer who can pretty dramatically shake up the battlefield, especially with his Ultimate, which basically consolidates allies and enemies together in one central clump for a frenzied exchange of blows. Alongside the new batch of seasonal cosmetics and events to dive into, it’s once again a good time to don your hero outfit and take on some matches.

Pikmin 4 released on Switch 2 this week (or upgraded to Switch 2 depending on how you look at it), and that's a good thing. Pikmin 4 is the best game in the series and the Switch 2 version is the best version. That's great for those who never finished the game (your save does transfer) or skipped Pikmin 4 when it released in 2023, but if you're looking for an excuse to return to the game and play new content, the Dandori Academy addition is underwhelming. You can read my full thoughts here.

Metaphor: ReFantazio, originally released in 2024, is a great RPG from the creators of Persona. And the Persona lineage is obvious throughout the full game. You have to pick and choose where and with whom you should be spending your time, all while a big world-saving RPG with a memorable party of characters plays out in the foreground.

It released this week for Switch 2 and it’s a game that I think would play well on a handheld device. It’s also just a good RPG to play if you missed it previously.

Fun fact: Metaphor: ReFantazio was the game we had lined up to be the next cover when we were temporarily shut down in in 2024. We went to the studio and had a cover drawn up and everything. You can read the full details of the cover story that never was right here.

You can also read Game Informer's review of Metaphor: ReFantazio by following the link.

As we enjoy the final week in a pre-GTA VI world, what better way to gird your loins for next week’s release, so to speak, than by revisiting the last adventures set in Rockstar’s take on Miami? 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a certified classic that, if you’ve never played it, offers nice foundational insight into what Vice City was like in the ’80s (spoiler: it was a lot like Scarface and Miami Vice). Best of all, Vice City is easily available on current platforms with modernized improvements to boot.

If you want to go even further back, chronologically speaking, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a prequel set two years before the events of Vice City. Maybe, in some extremely minute way, Vice City Stories lays narrative groundwork for GTA VI. It’s unlikely, but you never know. Originally released for PSP in 2006, Vice City Stories is trickier to play if you don’t own Sony's retired handheld or a PlayStation 2, which it was ported to in 2007. But if you can find the means, there’s no better time to check out this often overlooked chapter of Vice City’s history.

I usually hold off on early access games, to preserve my experience for the finished product, but I just couldn’t resist Slay the Spire 2. The co-op gameplay is an awesome, major change, but even just adding a couple of new characters and cards would have satisfied my cravings. To that end, this week’s free update adds a brand new character, the Fool, who I’m eager to test out.

FYI, this new character is only available on the game’s beta, so you’ll have to go into the game settings on steam, click Properties, then Game Versions & Betas, and then opt into the “public-beta” version of the game to check the new content out. The patch notes for this update specifically say, “We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch,” so expect frequent tweaks and a bit of a wait before the Fool joins the main Early Access branch. The new beta update also adds two more game modes: Dread and Blitz, which drastically alter your runs. If you want to wait a little while, the team at Mega Crit will refine these options into a more final form. But if you’re like me, more Slay the Spire 2 is more Slay the Spire 2, and I’m hopping in as soon as I can.

Monster Train 2 was one of my favorite games of last year, so I’m always glad to have a reason to jump back in. This week’s DLC, The Punished, is a perfect opportunity to do so, adding a new clan to the base game’s already packed roster. Since any clan can be combined with a second one to start a run, adding just one more option at the game’s start has an exponential effect, expanding the ways you can approach each attempt. As the DLC’s name implies, the new Punished clan gains buffs when taking damage, and you get new suite of cards that damages the whole playing field at once, harming foes and bolstering your allies. Even if you’re not checking out the DLC, the base game is absolutely worth picking up – just read my glowing review.

If you’ve been hankering for a new direction to go with your tabletop RPG group, may I recommend the incredibly versatile Cypher System from Monte Cook Games? The new Character Rulebook includes everything you need to get started, and set your adventures in virtually any fictional backdrop you can imagine, from hard sci-fi to gritty horror to high fantasy. Cypher’s polished approach to narrative-first and player-focused game sessions is much easier to pick up than many new rules systems, but it has enormous flexibility to deliver smart, creative, and exciting adventures that can help to change things up if your playing group has been in a rut.

#4043. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4041. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.
